title: Hyderabad reuses just 3.5% of the sewage it treats

slides.head: Hyderabad reuses just 3.5% of the sewage it treats
What happened
slides.body: A study and HMWSSB figures show most of Hyderabad's treated wastewater is not reused.

slides.head: Why it matters
slides.body: The city faces water shortages and growing tanker use amid El Niño and deficit rain.

slides.head: Did you know
slides.body: HMWSSB says its treatment capacity doubled from over 700 MLD in 2025 to about 1,400 MLD, yet ~30 MLD is recycled.

slides.head: What to watch
slides.body: HMWSSB tenders next month for supplying treated water to data centres and industries. Ask: Who should pay for pipelines carrying treated water to industries?

slides.head: Spill the tea, daily
slides.body: Hyderabad news in 30 seconds, with the numbers and the questions. Follow for tomorrow's drop: spillthetea.news

captions.instagram:
Hyderabad reuses just 3.5% of the sewage it treats

A 2025 study comparing Japan and India found Hyderabad reuses 27 MLD of the 772 MLD of sewage it treats, 3.5%, against a 20% central benchmark. HMWSSB plans tenders next month to supply treated water to data centres and industry.

Why it matters: The city faces water shortages and growing tanker use amid El Niño and deficit rain.

Source: Times of India. Image: Times of India
